_comment: Stage 7 - the NLP / semantic layer over the stage-5 extractions. Dense transformer embeddings in a persistent vector store, flood-domain NER, flood-type classification, event coreference, near-duplicate detection, source grounding, GeoNames linking and hybrid retrieval. Paths are absolute because every stage in this repo is; point them at your own trees. Nothing in here is a research constant - every threshold is meant to be swept.

paths._articles_comment: The article trees are not laid out consistently across years: 2021 lives under only_english2021/, and 2021 plus 2023-2025 nest their files one level deeper in articles/ while 2022 does not. Measured, not assumed - a missing override does not error, it silently yields empty bodies, which is what happened here until the per-year file counts were checked (2023: 16,503 files under articles/, none beside it).

runtime._comment: log_level is passed to logging.basicConfig by every script. seed fixes numpy/random sampling so annotation samples and medoid tie-breaks are reproducible.

embedding._comment: bge-base-en-v1.5: 109M params, 768-d, MTEB-strong for short English passages. Runs offline from the HF cache (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1). max_seq_length 256 covers the title + summary + locations string (p99 ~140 tokens). Query instruction is the model's documented retrieval prefix; documents get none.
embedding.query_instruction: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages:

chunking._comment: Optional second index over article bodies, used as evidence passages for the RAG answer step. Off by default: the event strings in flood_events are what coreference and event search need, and 74k bodies at ~4 chunks each is 300k extra vectors. Turn it on (or pass --chunks) when you want passage-level evidence retrieval. Chunks are cut at sentence boundaries, target_chars long, with overlap_chars carried into the next chunk so a fact split across a boundary survives in one piece somewhere.

index._comment: Chroma persistent collection with HNSW over cosine space. select=verifiable indexes only extractions with a date AND a location (the stage-5b gate); use flood to index every article the model accepted as one real flood, all for the whole corpus. flush_every controls how often embeddings.npy/ids.json are re-exported during a long run.

ner._comment: dslim/bert-base-NER is a generic CoNLL-2003 tagger (PER/ORG/LOC/MISC) - NOT a flood-trained model. ner.py runs it for the generic spans and then applies a flood-domain normalisation layer (lexicon + pattern rules + the stage-5 slots) to produce RIVER / FLOOD_TYPE / WEATHER_EVENT / INFRASTRUCTURE / CASUALTY / EVACUATION / DAMAGE. Entities carry a `source` field saying which of the two produced them; only model spans have a model confidence.

flood_type._comment: Flood-type classification. Two independent classifiers over the same text (title + summary + cause/trigger slots + optional body head): a transparent weighted-lexicon rule model, and an optional zero-shot pass through the local Qwen3-14B. `method` picks which runs; `agree` runs both and keeps the rule label unless the rule model abstains. The label set follows the standard hydrological typology; Unknown is a first-class answer and is what you get when no cue fires - never guess a type to fill the column.
flood_type._weights_comment: Cue weights are evidence strength, not frequency. 4 = the label is stated ('flash flood'); 3 = a mechanism only that type produces ('burst its banks', 'storm surge'); 2 = a strong associate ('danger mark', 'drainage system'); 1 = context that is worthless alone ('river', 'traffic'). min_score 2.0 is what makes weight-1 cues non-decisive on their own: a single mention of the word 'river' must never type an article as a River Flood, but 'river' plus 'water level rose' may.

clustering._comment: Event coreference: many articles -> one real-world flood. Candidates come from exact top_k cosine kNN over the event embeddings; each candidate pair is then scored by a weighted linear combination of five agreement signals and linked when the score clears link_threshold. Hard gates run first and can veto a link outright regardless of score. Weights sum to 1.0 by convention (nothing enforces it - the threshold moves with them). Set a weight to 0 to ablate that signal.

event._comment: Consolidated-event record. severity_bands are ordinal labels over the two counts the corpus reports most consistently; the first band whose floor is cleared by EITHER count wins. An event where neither count is known gets severity=null, not 'minor'. id_prefix + the first year of the event + a running number gives a stable, sortable event_id.

near_dup._comment: MinHash-LSH over w-word shingles of the article body. Stage 4 removed byte-identical copies with SHA-256; this catches syndicated rewrites, appended bylines and trimmed republications. jaccard_threshold 0.8 is conservative - two articles sharing 80% of their 5-word shingles are the same story, not two stories about the same flood. The `semantic` block is a separate, deliberately non-destructive pass: embedding cosine finds rewrites that share no shingles at all, and those pairs are reported as CANDIDATES only. Nothing is merged on embedding similarity alone.

grounding._comment: Every extracted field is checked back against the source text it came from. A count is grounded when the number appears in the body (as digits, with thousands separators, or as a spelled-out numeral); a date when the ISO date or any surface form of it appears; a location/river/country when the string, or its content tokens, appear. Flood type is grounded when the cue that fired is in the text. NER additionally confirms a location is something a tagger also reads as a place. Nothing here decides truth - it decides whether the extraction is SUPPORTED BY the article.

geocode._comment: Entity linking of free-text location strings to GeoNames ids with the offline geonamescache tables (cities >= 15k population, all countries, US states). The extracted country narrows candidates; remaining ties break on population, but only when the top candidate is ambiguity_ratio times larger than the runner-up. Otherwise the mention is emitted with status=ambiguous and every candidate listed - a wrong point on a map is worse than no point.

retrieval._comment: Hybrid retrieval. BM25 (rank_bm25, Okapi) over the same event strings the embeddings were built from, fused with dense Chroma results by reciprocal rank fusion. rrf_k=60 is the value from Cormack et al. 2009. The BM25 index is built once from events_meta.jsonl and cached as a pickle keyed by the row count, so repeat queries are instant.
retrieval._filter_depth_comment: Metadata filters the vector store cannot evaluate itself (a date range; a country substring) are applied after fusion, so a narrow filter can leave almost nothing. When one is present both retrievers fetch this many times deeper first. Costs one extra BM25 sort and a larger Chroma page; buys back the recall the filter would otherwise destroy.
retrieval._event_support_comment: When article hits are folded onto events, an event scores its BEST article times (1 + weight * ln(1 + matching articles)). Summing the articles instead lets a 90-article cluster of weak matches outrank a directly relevant single report - measured: 'Assam floods June 2021' returned the Yalta 2021 cluster first. Corroboration breaks ties; it does not decide the ranking.

rerank._comment: Optional cross-encoder reranking of the fused candidate list. Offline-first: nothing is ever downloaded. If `model` names a directory or an id already in the HF cache it is loaded and used; otherwise rerank.py reports that no local reranker is available and search falls back to the RRF order. Set model to a local path (e.g. a cached BAAI/bge-reranker-base) to switch it on.

llm._comment: Structured extraction / answering over RETRIEVED TEXT, through the same local Ollama server stage 5 uses. Embeddings are never sent to the model - the vector index selects which articles the model reads, the model only ever sees natural language. temperature 0 and format=json for reproducible, parseable output; think=false because qwen3 otherwise leaks its reasoning into the response.

eval._comment: Gold-set sampling and scoring. Samples are stratified by year and by the stage-5 verdict so a small annotation budget still covers positives, negatives and the borderline contains_flood-but-not-verifiable band. seed comes from runtime.seed unless overridden here.
